We also prompted a locally deployed generative large language model (LLM) on the same unimodal and multimodal inputs, without parameter updates. All were compared with InSilicoVA, the operational comparator representing current automated practice. We evaluated individual-level assignment, population-level agreement, calibration, and generalization across provinces in RSA, reporting these metrics rather than ranking pipelines on any one of them. RESULTS Every supervised pipeline improved on InSilicoVA by 8.5-15.9 percentage points in top-1 accuracy and 3.5-7.1 points in cause-specific mortality fraction (CSMF) accuracy. The narrative and structured pipelines performed similarly in aggregate but differed by cause: 63.9% of deaths received identical predictions, 11.6% were correct only from the narrative pipeline, and 13.6% only from the questionnaire pipeline, with the narrative pipeline more accurate for noncommunicable causes and the questionnaire pipeline for communicable causes. Against the unimodal approaches, the decision-fusion pipelines added 4.2-5.4 percentage points in top-1 accuracy, concentrated in the most common causes, whereas feature fusion with cross-modal attention improved the less common causes, adding 6.6 points (95% CI, 1.7-11.5) in balanced accuracy and 5.5 points (95% CI, 0.6-10.3) in macro F1. Feature fusion reached the highest CSMF accuracy (95.7%). Paired differences from the better unimodal representative ranged from -0.2 to +3.4 points, with all intervals including zero. The LLM exceeded InSilicoVA on individual-level metrics and reached the highest balanced accuracy of any pipeline (60.6%), while the supervised pipelines retained higher CSMF accuracy. Supervised pipelines had lower expected calibration error than InSilicoVA. Supervised gains held across all nine held-out provinces, including every top-1 comparison and nearly every macro F1 and CSMF comparison. CONCLUSIONS PLMs using narratives alone substantially improved on current best practice and matched ML pipelines using structured responses, while multiple multimodal strategies produced further gains in individual COD assignment. The zero-shot LLM showed particular strength on rare causes, whereas supervised pipelines better recovered the population cause distribution. These findings support incorporating narratives as a core input to automated VA systems and evaluating representative fusion strategies for the intended output. External validation across settings and age groups will support broader implementation.

items.title_en: Mutual Information in High-Dimensional Neural Coding
items.abstract_en: Estimating mutual information in large neural populations is limited by the exponential growth of possible neural response patterns. Here we apply a Monte Carlo framework to make this problem tractable by sampling from a conditionally independent population model fit from single-neuron responses. The estimator accurately recovers analytical ground truth, corrects finite-data bias, and scales to empirical recordings containing 100 to 10,000 neurons from visual cortex, hippocampus, and retina. Across systems, stimulus uncertainty decays exponentially with population size, revealing a simple scaling law for high-dimensional neural codes.

items.title_en: Documenting Trofinetide Treatment Phenotypes in Rett Syndrome with a Dual-LLM Consensus Pipeline
items.title_zh: 利用双LLM共识流程记录雷特综合征中曲非奈肽治疗表型
items.abstract_en: Objective: Trofinetide, approved in 2023 as the first Rett syndrome treatment, lacks scalable real-world monitoring because chart review is labor-intensive. We developed a dual large language model (LLM) consensus pipeline to extract 18 treatment-response phenotypes, comprising 4 adverse effects, 13 Rett clinical features, and medication refusal, from clinical notes. Materials and Methods: We analyzed 26,763 notes from 108 patients with confirmed sustained trofinetide exposure at Texas Children's Hospital. The pipeline filters notes by keyword, classifies each through two LLMs requiring consensus, and aggregates a patient-by-timepoint matrix. Architecture and prompt were selected on a diarrhea development set, then frozen and applied to the other 17 phenotypes with the phenotype definition substituted, as an out-of-sample test. The reported prompt comparison scores 183 expert-labeled cells. Results: A prompt requiring diarrhea to be active and severe performed best (84.2 $\pm$ 0.0% accuracy; F1 = 0.674), 47 percentage points above regular-expression matching ($p < 0.0001$). Expert reviewers judged six of the pipeline's calls per phenotype, three positive and three negative, and agreed with 90.2% (92/102). The 13 Rett clinical features are manifestations of the disorder itself rather than adverse effects of trofinetide. Gross and fine motor impairment, language/communication, and stereotypy were documented present in 92-100% of patients at every visit. Discussion: In-context LLM extraction captured multi-domain treatment responses. The outcome is documented presence at each visit, not a direction-of-change judgment. Conclusion: Coupling in-context LLM reasoning with a consensus architecture offers a scalable alternative to keyword and regular-expression extraction for real-world evidence, adapting to new phenotypes and medications through configuration alone.

items.title_en: Panoramic modelling of single-cell transcriptomes at scale with CellNet
items.title_zh: 基于CellNet的大规模单细胞转录组全景建模
items.abstract_en: Comprehensively characterizing cellular diversity is critical for understanding tissue development, identifying disease-associated populations and investigating gene programmes linked to specialized functions. Advances in single-cell profiling reveal additional cell-specific transcripts and molecular associations, yet many foundation models represent only a restricted portion of this increasingly rich molecular information. Here we present CellNet, which enables panoramic modelling of single-cell transcriptomes by integrating DNA-derived gene identities and measured RNA expression in a shared image representation. Pretrained on 231 million cell profiles spanning 40 species, CellNet improves rare-population and condition-associated state recognition in evaluated cohorts while retaining competitive general cell representations. It predicts withheld coding-gene expression and selected non-coding targets in total-RNA data, and recovers lineage-specific expression patterns in spatial measurements. Prediction also extends across species, including to targets without expression-pretraining exposure. Its gene representations retrieve known non-coding modules and developmental or neural programmes, including from sparsely detected RNA queries. Together, these results establish CellNet as a scalable framework for interpreting cellular diversity through increasingly comprehensive transcriptomic measurements.

items.title_en: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
items.title_zh: 利用大语言模型发现最先进的量子电路
items.abstract_en: Significant efforts are currently being directed toward the implementation of large-scale quantum information processors, but realizing useful quantum advantage also requires the development of efficient quantum algorithms. While for many practical problems the dominant resource costs are associated with a small set of computational primitives, optimizing them in the quantum setting presents unique challenges, including a reversibility constraint absent from ordinary classical computation. Here we introduce an evolutionary framework in which large language models (LLMs) propose circuit designs and an independent evaluator verifies and scores them. We apply this framework to tasks spanning numerical computation, chemistry, optimization, quantum simulation, and number theory. In seven of the eight tasks, the discovered circuits significantly reduce both Toffoli and qubit counts relative to the state of the art. In the eighth, the search discovers a new reversible architecture for prime-field modular inversion. By handling reversibility differently, the architecture makes divsteps -- a classical algorithm previously impractical for reversible integer arithmetic -- viable and substantially improves the Toffoli-qubit trade-off for modular inversion. These results open the door for evaluator-guided LLM co-design of new algorithmic structures for quantum computation.
items.abstract_zh: 本文提出由大语言模型提出量子电路设计、独立评估器验证打分的进化框架，并将其用于数值计算、化学、优化、量子模拟和数论等任务。八个任务中有七个发现的电路显著减少Toffoli门与量子比特数，优于现有最优；第八个任务发现素数域模逆的新可逆架构，使divsteps算法可行并改善Toffoli-量子比特权衡。结果表明评估器引导的LLM可协同设计量子计算新算法结构。
items.highlight_zh: LLM与独立评估器进化搜索发现更优量子电路
items.digest_zh: 研究问题：量子算法中少数计算原语主导资源成本，但量子情形优化它们受可逆性等独特约束。方法：构建进化框架，由大语言模型提出电路设计，独立评估器负责验证和打分，避免只依赖模型自评；在数值计算、化学、优化、量子模拟、数论等八类任务上搜索。结果：七类任务同时显著降低Toffoli门数和量子比特数，超过此前最优；第八类任务发现素数域模逆的新可逆架构，让原本不适合可逆整数运算的divsteps变得可行，并改善Toffoli-量子比特权衡。意义：说明LLM加自动评估器不仅能调参，还能发现新的算法结构，为量子计算协同设计提供通用路径。

items.title_en: Stability of Quantum LDPC States under Local Pauli Noise
items.title_zh: 局域Pauli噪声下量子LDPC态的稳定性
items.abstract_en: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes have a canonical mixed state---the normalized projector onto the code space---that lies at the intersection of quantum error correction and quantum many-body physics, yet the stability of its information-theoretic structure under local noise remains poorly understood. Recent progress on mixed-state phases of matter has identified the spatial decay of conditional mutual information (CMI) $I(A:C|B)$ as a key diagnostic of such stability, analogous to the role of the spectral gap for quantum ground states. We prove that, for the normalized code-projector state of a $\mathbb{Z}_d$ qLDPC stabilizer code under local Pauli noise, the CMI across a buffer $B$ separating $A$ from $C$ decays exponentially with the width of $B$ in two complementary noise regimes independent of system size. At weak noise, this holds for full-system tripartitions, where correlations between the two sides require an error cluster to cross the buffer, an exponentially unlikely event. At strong noise, exponential decay holds whenever the buffer supports no logical operator, since correlations can persist only along rare chains of buffer qudits that remain informative. Under an additional space-uniformity assumption, we establish the robustness of Levin--Wen topological entropy. On finite-dimensional lattices of size $n$, the weak-noise bound further implies a constant-layer quasi-local Petz recovery channel of range $O(\poly(\log n)/\varepsilon)$ that recovers the noiseless state within trace-distance error $\varepsilon$. Both CMI bounds apply to general qLDPC interaction graphs, including geometries where such constant-depth quasi-local recovery need not exist. Thus, the exponential decay of the noise-induced CMI provides a general criterion for mixed-state phase stability.
items.abstract_zh: 量子低密度奇偶校验（qLDPC）码的码空间投影态连接量子纠错与多体物理，但其在局域噪声下的稳定性尚不清楚。本文证明，在局域Pauli噪声下，Z_d qLDPC稳定子码的归一化码投影态中，跨越缓冲区的条件互信息在弱噪声与强噪声两个区域均随缓冲区宽度指数衰减且与系统尺寸无关；弱噪声适用于全系统三分割，强噪声在缓冲区不含逻辑算子时成立。空间均匀假设下还证明Levin-Wen拓扑熵鲁棒。有限网格上弱噪声界给出常层数准局域Petz恢复信道，范围O(poly(log n)/ε)，可在迹距离ε内恢复无噪声态。结果适用于一般qLDPC图。
items.highlight_zh: 证明qLDPC码投影态的CMI在局域噪声下指数衰减
items.digest_zh: 研究问题：qLDPC码的码空间归一化投影态是量子纠错与多体物理的交叉对象，但局域噪声下其信息论结构是否稳定仍不清楚。方法：以条件互信息CMI跨越缓冲区的空间衰减作为稳定性诊断，分析Z_d qLDPC稳定子码在局域Pauli噪声下的码投影态。结果：弱噪声下，全系统三分割的CMI随缓冲区宽度指数衰减；强噪声下，只要缓冲区不支持逻辑算子，CMI也指数衰减，且两者都与系统尺寸无关。在额外空间均匀性假设下，Levin-Wen拓扑熵保持鲁棒。有限维网格上，弱噪声界还给出常层数准局域Petz恢复信道，范围O(poly(log n)/ε)，可在迹距离ε内恢复无噪声态。意义：给出混合态稳定性的通用判据，并连接量子纠错与多体相。

items.title_en: Magic in quantum trajectory unravelings of noisy random quantum circuits
items.title_zh: 含噪随机量子电路量子轨迹展开中的魔法
items.abstract_en: The quantum-trajectory description of a noisy quantum circuit is not unique: every Kraus representation of the noise channel defines a different unraveling, i.e., a different ensemble of pure states that averages to the same density matrix. While all unravelings share the same expectation values of observables, they generally differ in the amount of quantum resources carried by the individual trajectories. Here we study non-stabilizerness, or magic, quantified by the stabilizer Rényi entropy, in quantum-trajectory unravelings of Haar-random and $T$-doped random Clifford brickwork circuits subject to local dephasing noise of strength $p$. The canonical unraveling in terms of Pauli jumps is Clifford and leaves magic untouched, so that trajectories retain the Haar-random value of non-stabilizerness. Exploring the full two-parameter family of minimal unravelings, we find that the trajectory-averaged magic can be substantially reduced by a state-independent choice of Kraus operators, and that the optimal choice is not in general the projective-measurement unraveling, but a two-outcome generalized measurement in which the Kraus operators correspond to a weak measurement of the noisy qubit. The optimal unraveling reduces the extensive magic density of the trajectories by a $p$-dependent factor without altering its linear scaling with system size. At the same time, it produces a very broad distribution of magic over trajectories, with a sizable fraction of trajectories retaining Haar-random magic. Since the cost of stabilizer-based classical simulation grows exponentially with the magic of the state, these high-magic trajectories, rather than the average, control the simulation cost. Our results delineate the potential and the limitations of unraveling optimization as a route to the classical simulation of noisy quantum dynamics with stabilizer methods.
items.abstract_zh: 含噪量子电路的量子轨迹描述不唯一：噪声信道的每种Kraus表示对应不同纯态系综，平均后密度矩阵相同，但单条轨迹携带的量子资源不同。本文以稳定子Rényi熵量化魔法，研究Haar随机与T掺杂随机Clifford砖墙电路在局域退相位噪声下的轨迹展开。Pauli跳跃的典范展开是Clifford的，不改变魔法。探索最小展开双参数族发现，状态无关的Kraus选择可显著降低轨迹平均魔法；最优常为两结果广义弱测量而非投影测量。它按依赖噪声强度的因子降低广延魔法密度但不改线性标度，并产生宽分布，仍有不少高魔法轨迹。由于稳定子模拟成本随魔法指数增长，这些高魔法轨迹决定模拟成本。
items.highlight_zh: 优化Kraus展开可降平均魔法但高魔法轨迹主导模拟成本
items.digest_zh: 研究问题：噪声信道的不同Kraus展开给出不同纯态轨迹系综，虽然平均密度矩阵相同，但轨迹携带的魔法可能不同，从而影响基于稳定子的经典模拟成本。方法：对Haar随机和T掺杂随机Clifford砖墙电路施加局域退相位噪声，用稳定子Rényi熵量化非稳定子性，并扫描最小展开的双参数族。结果：Pauli跳跃的典范展开本身是Clifford的，不改变魔法，轨迹保留Haar随机值；状态无关的Kraus算符选择可显著降低轨迹平均魔法，最优一般不是投影测量，而是对应含噪量子比特弱测量的两结果广义测量。最优展开按依赖噪声强度p的因子降低广延魔法密度，但不改变其随系统尺寸的线性标度，并造成很宽的魔法分布，仍有相当比例轨迹保持高魔法。意义：由于模拟成本由最难轨迹控制，展开优化有潜力但无法简单消除高魔法轨迹。

items.title_en: Magna: simulating magic state factories as cheaply as Clifford circuits
items.title_zh: Magna：以与Clifford电路同等低廉的成本模拟魔法态工厂
items.abstract_en: Classical simulation of magic state factories, including distillation, cultivation, and code switching, is challenging because of their substantial non-Clifford content. We introduce $\texttt{magna}$ (magic-state-factory assessment via global network algebra), a classical simulator that simulates such protocols as cheaply as Clifford circuits. $\texttt{magna}$ expresses the figures of merit of a protocol, namely the acceptance rate and the fidelity of the accepted states, as tensor networks, which it reduces globally by exploiting a structural correspondence with transversal gates on quantum codes. $\texttt{magna}$ further supports feedforward conditioned on arbitrary functions of mid-circuit measurement outcomes, including decoder outputs. We simulate Bravyi--Haah distillation with up to 100 output magic states at a cost that does not grow exponentially in the number of outputs, and achieve state-of-the-art sampling times for distance-5 magic state cultivation on both color codes and RP$^2$ surface codes. Finally, we validate nonlinear feedforward on a logical-level distillation protocol with 15 rounds of decoder-dependent feedforward. $\texttt{magna}$ aims to contribute to the key infrastructure for the large-scale evaluation and optimization of magic state factories.

items.title_en: Classical Capacity of Single-Mode Bosonic Gaussian Channels
items.title_zh: 单模玻色高斯信道的经典容量
items.abstract_en: The classical capacity of a noisy optical channel is the maximum rate at which information can be transmitted reliably, given a constraint on the mean input energy. For the ubiquitous bosonic Gaussian channels, which include standard models of loss and noise in fibre and free-space optical links, determining this rate requires addressing whether entanglement between channel uses or non-Gaussian signals can outperform Gaussian encodings. More precisely, the question is whether the energy-constrained Holevo information is additive across arbitrarily many channel uses and coincides with its Gaussian counterpart. We answer these fundamental questions in the affirmative for every single-mode bosonic Gaussian channel at every input energy. Namely, we prove that independently prepared Gaussian states with Gaussian-distributed random displacements achieve the capacity, including in the low-energy regime where squeezing the signals competes with encoding information in their displacement. Our proof connects an entanglement inequality to a sharp, additive lower bound on output entropy. We then characterise communication above capacity: under a strict total photon-number cutoff, the probability of correct decoding decreases exponentially with the number of channel uses, and we derive explicit bounds on the decay exponent. When only the mean photon number is constrained, a simple energy-rescaling formula determines exactly the entire asymptotic rate--error trade-off: the capacity at mean photon number $N$ and allowed average decoding error $ε$ equals the vanishing-error capacity at mean photon number $N/(1-ε)$. Together, these results identify the ultimate limits of classical communication for some of the most fundamental models of optical communication.

items.title_en: Adding Temperature to the Adiabatic Connection: Hybrid Functionals for Static and Dynamic Correlation
items.title_zh: 为绝热连接引入温度：用于静态和动态相关能的杂化泛函
items.abstract_en: Capturing static and dynamic electron correlation simultaneously at manageable computational cost remains a key challenge in electronic structure theory. Motivated by the recurring role of effective temperature in self-consistent field methods we extend the adiabatic connection mechanism from density functional theory to include a temperature dimension. This gives rise to thermally enhanced hybrid functionals, in which static correlation is captured via fractional occupations generated by an effective "correlation temperature" within thermal Hartree-Fock, while dynamic correlation is described by established density functional approximations. The framework formally unifies information-density matrix functional theory (i-DMFT) and thermally-assisted-occupation (TAO-)DFT as special cases, clarifying their theoretical basis and the respective prescriptions for the temperature parameter. We assess the performance of several thermally enhanced hybrids for different cases where i-DMFT was previously shown to fail. Furthermore, we discuss and test different schemes for determining the correlation temperature and investigate the accuracy of different such choices for a benchmark set derived from biphenyl. The results help to clarify the achievable balance of accuracy, generality, and efficiency, establishing thermally enhanced hybrids as a systematic route toward low-cost treatment of both correlation types.

items.title_en: SynDebug: A Framework to Debug Logic Bugs in Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Programs
items.title_zh: SynDebug：用于调试容错量子计算程序中逻辑错误的框架
items.abstract_en: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) introduces substantial systems-level complexity through quantum error correction (QEC), making debugging FTQC programs challenging. Existing quantum debugging approaches primarily target logical-level circuits and do not naturally support debugging within realistic FTQC execution flows. We present SynDebug, the first systems-level debugging framework for FTQC programs. SynDebug introduces lightweight assertion-based debugging primitives that operate directly within encoded FTQC infrastructures while avoiding additional logical surface area and minimizing temporal overhead. We evaluate SynDebug across multiple QEC code families, code distances, and encoded workloads, including state preparation, entanglement validation, and Shor-style programs. Our results demonstrate that SynDebug enables practical FTQC debugging with an average 1.8% additional circuit depth overhead (0% in most cases) and no measurable increase in the logical error rate, showing that systems-level debugging for large-scale FTQC applications is both feasible and practical.

items.title_en: Constrained dissipation and the lifetime of quantum many-body scars
items.title_zh: 受约束耗散与量子多体疤痕的寿命
items.abstract_en: We investigate the fate of quantum many-body scars in the PXP model subject to Markovian dissipation. We show that when local jump operators respect the same symmetries of the Hamiltonian the full Liouvillian spectrum displays a tower of states with properties analogous to standard quantum scars: large overlaps with Néel states and equally spaced gaps in the imaginary part of the eigenvalues, set by a single frequency. Whether the long-time dynamics is dominated by scars is determined by the real parts of the eigenvalues, which are set by the ratio between the two relaxation rates $γ_{\pm}$ describing spin flips down-to-up or up-to-down respectively. For asymmetric dissipation ($γ_+ > γ_-$) the scarred eigenvalues have the smallest real parts: the resulting enhanced fidelity oscillations are further stabilized by staggered jump operators. In contrast, replacing the full projection operator in the dissipators with a partial one breaks the symmetries of the problem and is seen to destroy dissipative scars altogether.

items.title_en: Programmable all-to-all entangling gates for cavity-coupled atoms
items.title_zh: 用于腔耦合原子的可编程全连接纠缠门
items.abstract_en: Fault tolerant quantum computers greatly benefit from having both high fidelity entangling gates and a non-local qubit connectivity. However, most entangling gates for neutral atoms are local, requiring separated atoms to be moved using optical tweezers to yield entanglement between them. Here, we design a high fidelity Mølmer Sørensen-like entangling gate between neutral atoms coupled to a photonic cavity, enabling a programmable all-to-all connectivity through the shared cavity coupling. The gate is both robust to changes in cavity photon number, and enables selective entanglement between any subset of separated atoms through local laser addressing. This eliminates the need to physically move atoms to perform the gate, and therefore motional errors and erasure are suppressed. Using experimentally realistic parameters we demonstrate gate fidelities exceeding $F > 0.99$, with higher fidelities achievable through optimal control of the pump amplitudes.

items.title_en: Efficient quantum simulation of unitary gates based on atomic ensembles
items.title_zh: 基于原子系综的酉门高效量子模拟
items.abstract_en: We develop a technique to perform efficient unitary time evolution of a general spin Hamiltonian based on the system with identical qubits, as naturally realized by permutation symmetric atomic ensembles. We employ Cartan decomposition method to the associated Hamiltonian Lie algebra and construct the symmetry adapted generators to implement unitary operator of the ensemble Hamiltonian. This enables the compact circuit representations of the system dynamics in terms of experimentally accessible collective spin operations and exploits the Dicke basis structure of the ensembles as an effective qudit representation. We benchmark Cartan based evolution against both exact time evolution and the Suzuki Trotter product formula. Our results show that the Cartan protocol accurately reproduces the operator dynamics, spin expectation values, and fluctuation observables with zero error that are substantially smaller than those obtained through Trotterization while maintaining an optimized circuit structure. In addition, scaling analysis with the ensemble size demonstrates that the Cartan error remains independent of the atom number while the corresponding Trotter error increases with the system size, highlighting the improved efficiency of the Cartan approach for a larger system size.

items.title_en: Classification of bipartite observables III: simplicity, mixtures and quantum error correction
items.title_zh: 二分可观测量的分类 III：简单性、混合与量子纠错
items.abstract_en: The paradigm of a simple unstable theory in the sense of Shelah is the theory of the random graph, the Fraïssé limit of the finite graphs. Quantum error correction has a paradigm of its own, and we show that it is the counterpart of the random graph: the Pauli group on countably many qubits, taken modulo phases and with commutation as its relation, is the Fraïssé limit of the finite alternating spaces over the two-element field, and its form computes the syndromes of stabilizer codes. Seen through this correspondence, simplicity theory turns out to be a theory of error correction. Clifford encoding circuits implement the homogeneity of the Pauli group, forking recognizes the logical errors, and the independence theorem of Kim and Pillay is the gluing of syndromes. The two paradigms look alike as first-order structures, and they part company only when observables enter. Each defines a bipartite observable, and we prove that, once preparations are mixed, both acquire the tree property of the second kind in real-valued logic. They reach it by different roads, however, and we show that the probes decide which. The probes of the Pauli observable are the Pauli channels; for them the indicator of each syndrome sector is the difference of the responses of two uniform mixtures, and actual mixtures already witness the tree. The probes of the Rado observable see only marginals; conditions given by actual mixtures remain compatible on disjoint blocks, and the tree must be sought among idealized preparations.

items.title_en: Energetics of Fault-Tolerant Spin-Qubit Quantum Computation
items.title_zh: 容错自旋量子比特量子计算的能量学
items.abstract_en: Semiconductor spin qubits offer a promising route to compact and scalable quantum computers, combining long coherence times in isotopically purified silicon with compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing. Beyond computational speedup, their energy efficiency is an important consideration for future large-scale systems. We evaluate the power and energy requirements of a Loss-DiVincenzo spin-qubit quantum computer by analyzing the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) and benchmarking it against the classical Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). We develop a detailed energy budget, identifying cryogenic cooling as the dominant baseline contribution before quantum error correction (QEC). The comparison between the QFT and the classical FFT reveals that, for any quantum workload operating under a polynomially bounded sampling regime, the crossover in energy consumption occurs at smaller problem sizes than the crossover in execution time. Thus, quantum computing can become energetically competitive before achieving a speedup in execution time. We then incorporate surface-code QEC and analyze the energy costs of QEC cycles, gate synthesis, and decoding. At scale, instrumentation and decoding become dominant contributions, while cryogenic cooling imposes a constraint on scalability. We show that optimizing the control-signal demultiplexing ratio can reduce the overall energy cost by approximately two orders of magnitude. For a system with about one million physical qubits, we estimate a power consumption of approximately 100 kW, at least one order of magnitude below that of today's highest-performance classical computing systems.

items.title_en: Connectivity Bounds for GHZ Graphs
items.title_zh: GHZ 图的连通性界
items.abstract_en: Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states are multipartite entangled quantum states that play a central role in quantum information theory, with applications in quantum communication, cryptography, and distributed quantum computing. A major experimental goal is to create high-dimensional GHZ states using multiple entangled parties. Krenn, Gu and Zeilinger discovered a surprising bridge between these quantum-optical experiments and graph theory: certain photonic experiments can be represented by edge-coloured, edge-weighted graphs, and the dimension of the produced GHZ state equals the number of feasible monochromatic inherited vertex colourings. This led Krenn and Gu to conjecture that every GHZ graph with more than four vertices has dimension at most $2$. A counterexample would give a new high-dimensional multipartite GHZ construction, while a proof would clarify fundamental resource limitations in quantum optics. It is known that the conjecture holds for graphs of vertex connectivity at most $2$ [MFCS 2024], and that simple GHZ graphs with $n>4$ vertices have dimension less than $n/\sqrt{2}$ [Quantum 2024]. However, no general upper bound depending only on vertex connectivity was known. We prove that every simple connected GHZ graph $G$ with at least four vertices has dimension at most $2^{κ(G)-1}+\binom{κ(G)}{2}$, where $κ(G)$ is the vertex connectivity of $G$. We also prove new bounds in terms of edge connectivity and maximum degree.

items.title_en: Frequency comb stability, bistability, and self-starting in normal dispersion microresonators
items.title_zh: 正常色散微谐振腔中频率梳的稳定性、双稳性与自启动
items.abstract_en: Recent work has demonstrated that it is possible to generate frequency combs in normal dispersion microresonators by taking advantage of fabricated mode coupling that induces a mode split. In particular, photonic crystal resonators periodically modulate the microresonator's width, which geometrically creates mode coupling. In contrast to frequency combs generated by microresonators in the anomalous dispersion regime, which are typically generated using bright solitons, the frequency combs generated by normal dispersion regime microresonators are dark pulses that are commonly referred to as dark solitons or platicons. In this work, we examine the linear stability of platicons in the pump-detuning and pump-power parameter space as the mode split strength and cavity dispersion is varied. Our work reveals a broad region of stability for platicons. Our work also reveals the existence of fingers at high power at whose boundaries a sharp transition occurs and inside of which platicon solutions are bistable. Finally, we investigate the overlap of the region where platicons are stable with the region where continuous waves are modulationally unstable, and it is possible for a platicon to self-start. Simulations show that platicons consistently self-start inside this region.

items.title_en: Gyrators for superconducting circuit design
items.title_zh: 用于超导电路设计的回转器
items.abstract_en: Assuming only the solubility of Kirchhoff's laws, the conservation of energy, and the form of the constitutive relations, we present a flux-charge symmetric Hamiltonian formalism that always admits a symplectic reduction for nonsingular, well-posed circuits involving gyrators, inductors, and capacitors (LCG circuits) with arbitrary non-linearity. The formalism introduces a notion of circuit duality on non-linear non-reciprocal circuits and a family of point transformations that inserts, removes, and moves reciprocal elements across gyrators while preserving the Hamiltonian spectrum. With these transformations, we extend Tellegen's classic result that gyrators make reciprocal elements behave as their dual to non-linear reciprocal elements such as the Josephson junction and quantum phase slip. Furthermore, we present conditions under which non-reciprocal circuits can be transformed to dynamically equivalent reciprocal circuits.

items.title_en: Putting a Temperature on Electron Correlation
items.title_zh: 为电子关联赋予温度
items.abstract_en: It is common wisdom that a better understanding of how to quantify electron correlation should lead to more efficient treatments of the correlation problem. Here, we not only substantiate this view but turn it into a concrete, systematic framework for ground states. Since prominent correlation measures such as the nonfreeness depend only on the one-particle reduced density matrix, modeling the correlation energy as a function of such a measure naturally places the framework within reduced density matrix functional theory, while keeping the cost at mean-field level. Strikingly, the variable conjugate to the measure emerges as a ``correlation temperature'', thereby connecting correlation measures, functional theory, and effective temperatures. The framework rationalizes methods such as i-DMFT, and we illustrate its key concepts analytically for the Hubbard dimer and numerically for small molecular systems. This brings a fundamental question within reach: how much of the correlation problem can be solved at mean-field cost?

items.title_en: Patchwork: automated lattice surgery and space-time partitioning for real-time decoding
items.title_zh: Patchwork：面向实时解码的自动化晶格手术与时空划分
items.abstract_en: We introduce patchwork, a lattice-surgery compiler for arbitrary multi-qubit Pauli measurements on a prescribed narrow-corridor two-dimensional surface-code layout. Systematic geometric rules simplify stabilizer placement and gate scheduling, including for logical $Y$ measurements implemented using twist defects. We introduce measurement circuits and schedules that, together with protruding lobes of $Y$-extension patches, preserve the full effective code distance for all numerically tested code distances. To support parallel decoding, we develop a wavefront algorithm that partitions merged lattice-surgery patches into space-time commit, buffer, and cleanup regions. Simulations of three sequential multi-qubit Pauli measurements acting on ten logical qubits show that staged decoding achieves total failure probabilities close to those of monolithic decoding over the parameters tested. These methods provide an automated framework for fault-tolerant lattice surgery and a route toward scalable, real-time decoding.

items.title_en: Operational Limits of Gravity-Mediated Entanglement
items.title_zh: 引力介导纠缠的操作极限
items.abstract_en: Tests of gravity-mediated entanglement aim to determine whether two massive objects in spatial superposition can become entangled through their mutual gravitational interaction. In an ideal model, the two objects are often treated as pointlike branches, but real wave packets have a finite width and are also exposed to dephasing and residual non-gravitational forces. We study these effects in a two-branch gravitational cat-state model with Gaussian wave packets. The Newtonian interaction is averaged over the finite wave-packet width, and spatially correlated dephasing is included phenomenologically. We then ask a practical question: when does the generated state remain useful rather than merely entangled? To answer this, we examine Bell violation, teleportation fidelity, coherent information, Fisher information, and state distinguishability. We find finite parameter windows where the same state is Bell-nonlocal and teleportation-useful, but these windows shrink as the wave packets become broader or the dephasing becomes stronger. We also show that a residual electrostatic branch interaction can coherently cancel the gravitational nonlocal phase and strongly suppress the operational signal. The results identify finite-width and electrostatic tolerance boundaries that should be considered in future tests of gravity-mediated entanglement.

items.title_en: Bubble-Sort Exchange Networks: Symmetry Selection Rules and Language-Model Distillation on Exchange-Only Spin Chains
items.abstract_en: On a chain of exchange-coupled quantum dots a Heisenberg exchange pulse of area pi is a SWAP, so the parallel bubble-sort SWAP network of superconducting chains is native to exchange-only (EO) spin qubits, and any other pulse area fuses routing with an entangling interaction. We build a variational "bubble-sort exchange network" (odd-even transposition, one parameter per pulse) and study it as a Born machine read out by Pauli spin blockade. Exchange conserves total spin, so the reachable readout distributions are fixed by the total-spin content of the initial product state. For the two-spin singlet-triplet encoding we derive a selection rule -- outcomes with k triplet pairs are bounded by the initial weight in sectors S <= k (S = 0 excluded for k = 1) -- and prove by a transportation argument that it is also sufficient: the reachable distributions form the polytope cut out by the rule, and its total-variation floor is attained. Products of singlets and T0's forbid whole outcome classes; the Neel state forbids none; the three-spin EO code has no floor. We then distil, in noise-free simulation, next-token distributions of GPT-2 over restricted vocabularies into the network, with matrix-product-state (MPS) Born machines as classical control. At six logical qubits the three-spin chain reaches KL = 0.011 nat at depth N and 0.004 at 2N, below the bond-dimension-4 MPS; the two-spin chain from the Neel state reaches 0.014 at 2N and 0.004 at 3N, against 0.28-1.5 from singlet/triplet products for the first teacher. Final states lie largely outside the code space: leakage is a resource, not an error. No arrangement of disjoint pulses meets every pair in fewer than N-1 rounds, and at depth 2N the chain distils as well as a 2D array or non-local couplings. Sector-restricted simulation extends this to 10-14 logical qubits (up to 30 dots).

items.title_en: Generalized $m$-body mean-field projections for classical simulation of $d$-dimensional Heisenberg-picture dynamics
items.abstract_en: Classical simulation of quantum many-body dynamics is challenged by the rapid growth of operator complexity, particularly in higher dimensions where tensor-network methods become increasingly demanding. We develop state-adapted Pauli-weight propagation based on generalized $m$-body mean-field projections, which compress many-body observables into optimal low-body representations in a covariance geometry induced by the initial state. Combined with adaptive Krylov-like restricted Heisenberg dynamics, this provides an alternative to conventional Hilbert--Schmidt Pauli-weight truncation. We derive necessary and conditional sufficient bounds on low-body approximation accuracy using standard operator complexity measures and characterize possible dynamical failure mechanisms of the state-adapted method. Numerical benchmarks demonstrate substantial state-dependent accuracy gains, while identifying regimes of reduced accuracy or violations of Pauli spectral bounds. For a three-dimensional system of $80$ interacting spins, our method achieves strong body-order convergence, close agreement with independently converging tensor-network simulations, and substantially smaller sparse Pauli representations. These results establish state-adapted Pauli propagation as a promising approach to classical simulation of higher-dimensional coherent many-body dynamics.

items.title_en: Energetic channels in finite many-body quantum charging
items.abstract_en: We examine how a finite many-body system can function as an effective charger for a single-qubit quantum battery, using the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model as a paradigmatic setting. As our figure of merit, we consider the battery ergotropy while explicitly resolving the energetic flows across the composite system. In the absence of intra-charger interactions, we show that the generation of non-zero ergotropy is controlled by the competition between collective coupling and spectral mismatch. We further demonstrate that even passive positive-temperature charger states can generate finite battery ergotropy, provided the charger is sufficiently large and sufficiently hot. Intra-charger interactions restructure the charger spectrum and qualitatively modify the available energetic pathways. While they can enhance the amount of energy accessible for charging, they can simultaneously divert energy into internal many-body and battery-charger interaction channels, producing an energetic impedance to direct charger-to-battery transfer. Consequently, battery ergotropy alone is insufficient to characterize an effective many-body charger: the useful work generated and its energetic provenance must be assessed together.

items.title_en: Loss-independent time-delay estimation via Hong-Ou-Mandel photon bunching detection
items.abstract_en: In this work we study the application of two-photon correlated quantum states for high-precision time estimation. To achieve this, photon pairs were fed into a Hong-Ou-Mandel polarization interferometer to generate N00N entangled states with $N = 2$. Two- and four-detector schemes were considered, and the achievable time estimation precision of each was studied, with particular emphasis on the system's Fisher information in each case. Our results reveal that using a four-detector scheme, enabling the measurement of both coincidence and photon-bunching terms, achieves the maximum precision given by the quantum Fisher information, without the need of characterizing system losses. We also show that correlations between repetitions arise due to systematic errors, limiting the precision enhancement that can be obtained by increasing the number of repetitions. Taking these correlations into account, we show that the four-detector scheme outperforms the two-detector scheme in the precision of time-delay estimation. With the experimentally determined calibration uncertainties, the four-detector scheme improves the dispersion by a factor of 2 for the repetitions performed, reaching up to a factor of 4 as both schemes approach their systematic floors.

items.title_en: Thermal activation of photon catalysis in difference-intensity Mach-Zehnder interferometry with squeezed thermal light
items.abstract_en: Realistic non-Gaussian operations, which can be implemented by mixing a nonclassical Gaussian state with a Fock state at a beam splitter and then heralding on a photon-number-resolving detector, are known to improve phase estimation in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer. The existing studies have considered the single-mode squeezed vacuum for difference-intensity and parity detection, and the two-mode squeezed thermal state for parity detection alone as the initial Gaussian resources. However, a real squeezer in the lab actually produces single-mode squeezed thermal light, which has not been studied in a coherent-plus-resource interferometer. We take up this case and using the phase space Wigner picture, we obtain the heralded state produced by photon subtraction, addition and catalysis on a single-mode squeezed thermal resource, and evaluate the corresponding phase sensitivities. Single-photon catalysis, which is useless on squeezed vacuum, becomes a useful operation for any thermal occupation above $\nth\simeq0.2$, and since it heralds with a probability near one-half, it turns out to be the best success-weighted operation over the whole thermal range. In the vacuum limit our results reproduce the known hierarchy, where two-photon catalysis is the best operation. The quantum Fisher information computations confirms that thermal noise enhances the phase information encoded in the catalyzed state, demonstrating that difference-intensity detection closely approaches the ultimate precision bound across most operational regimes, and, together with a loss analysis, verifies the robustness of the effect.

items.title_en: Quantum control of solid state qubits via Reinforcement Learning
items.title_zh: 通过强化学习实现固态量子比特的量子控制
items.abstract_en: The use of reinforcement learning (RL) in the design of quantum control strategies for pulse level control of NISQ era quantum devices is attracting growing interest. Model-free RL, not requiring preexisting knowledge of the physical system, acts as a black-box optimization tool well suited for noisy devices. In this work, we provide a simulation-based analysis of the performance of model-free RL for state preparation and qubit gate design in a challenging setup: indirect control of NV nuclear spins in a spin-bath. In particular, the spin-bath is modeled via the generalized cluster correlation expansion accounting for magnetic impurities and intra-bath interactions. We analyze the performance of the RL agents by performing simulations with minimally observable environments and noisy, sparse rewards as introduced in (Phys. Rev. X 12, 011059), and compare them to other state-of-the-art black-box optimization tools.

items.title_en: A complete classification of perfect state transfer in Grover walks on abelian Cayley graphs
items.abstract_en: We completely classify connected Cayley graphs over finite abelian groups that exhibit perfect state transfer in Grover walks. First, we show that a Cayley graph over any finite group exhibiting perfect state transfer has valency $1$, $2$, or $4$. For valency $4$, we prove that an abelian Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(Γ,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if $S=\{a,-a,a+h,-a+h\}$, where $h$ has order $2$, and $4\nmid |Γ|/2$. Combining this characterization with the valency-one and valency-two cases, we explicitly determine all pairs $(Γ,S)$ for which $\operatorname{Cay}(Γ,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer. Our results extend the classification of circulant graphs of valency at most four obtained by Kubota and Yoshino [Circulant graphs with valency up to 4 that admit perfect state transfer in Grover walks, \emph{J. Comb. Theory Ser. A.}, 216 (2025) 106064] to Cayley graphs over arbitrary finite abelian groups and to all valencies.

items.title_en: Jianmu-Q: Bridging Quantum Field Theory and Quantum Hardware with AI Agents
items.abstract_en: Quantum computing offers a promising approach to non-perturbative simulations of quantum field theories, particularly for real-time dynamics and systems affected by the sign problem. Yet translating continuum field theories into quantum computations remains a challenging interdisciplinary task. Here we introduce \texttt{Jianmu-Q}, a multi-agent framework that transforms natural-language descriptions of quantum field theories into quantum simulation workflows. Specialized agents handle theoretical formulation, lattice discretization, qubit mapping, and circuit design, while physical consistency checks and independent numerical calculations provide validation throughout the workflow. We benchmark the framework on three field theories of increasing complexity: the $(1+1)$-dimensional Nambu--Jona-Lasinio and Schwinger models, and a $(2+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory. Across these systems, noiseless quantum-circuit simulations converge toward independent exact-diagonalization and tensor-network results, while selected circuits are executed on IBM quantum hardware, demonstrating an end-to-end, validation-guided approach to quantum simulation of field theories.

items.title_en: ZZ-Free bSWAP Gates under Strong Driving in Far-Detuned Fixed-Frequency Transmons
items.abstract_en: Far-detuned frequency allocations in fixed-frequency superconducting processors mitigate spectral crowding but constrain cross-resonance interactions at practical drive amplitudes. Here, we demonstrate that a single strong drive induces a large $XX-YY$ interaction in the far-detuned regime, while a weak second tone tunes the accompanying $ZZ$ phase. The interaction realizes a 150-ns $\sqrt{\mathrm{bSWAP}}$ gate, which can directly prepare a maximally entangled state from the ground state. For the implementations on the same qubit pair at matched drive strengths, cross resonance gives a shorter CNOT operation, while $\sqrt{\mathrm{bSWAP}}$ gives a 33% shorter SWAP operation with a higher IRB fidelity. The multilevel theory further predicts a regime where stronger driving can yield a speed advantage for CNOT as well, a possibility absent in the two-level model. As an application of the $XX-YY$ interaction, we also demonstrate two-spin squeezing beyond the standard quantum limit through two-axis countertwisting. The interaction realized here complements cross resonance and offers a route to efficient gate synthesis and quantum simulation of interacting spin systems.

items.title_en: Synergistic charging of a quantum battery via Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and non-Markovian noise
items.abstract_en: Protecting quantum batteries from environmental noise remains a challenge. Using exact Burshtein-Kubo equations, we study a two-spin quantum battery with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) coupling under indepen dent local longitudinal random telegraph noise (RTN). At a fixed effective noise scale, the DM-assisted slow switching protocol yields a superadditive transient ergotropy gain and near-maximal ergotropy during the initial charging stage, while the no-DM slow-switching control reaches comparable ergotropy only in a later revival. A finite superadditive region persists at fixed RTN amplitude, with protocol-dependent location and gain. In the Ising model, the enhancement is nonmonotonic in DM strength, with intermediate coupling giving near-optimal performance. Dressed-channel analysis associates this enhancement with changes in transition frequencies and longitudinal-noise matrix elements that reduce slow-RTN spectral weight. Superadditivity also persists in the tested anisotropic XY model.

items.title_en: Opinion bubbles in the quantum Buridan's ass problem
items.abstract_en: The quantum Buridan's ass problem concerns a network of interconnected nodes in which transitions between the nodes are governed by the laws of quantum mechanics. In such situations interference between probability amplitudes plays a key role in determining whether the probability of leaving the initial node is large or small and also the speed at which the associated transitions occur. In this paper we extend this idea to consider transitions between one given set of coupled nodes and the remainder of the network. We have in mind a quantum analogy to changing an opinion, in which the initially occupied set of nodes is one opinion bubble, with the remaining parts of the network corresponding to a different opinion. We find that quantum interference again plays a crucial role in the dynamics. A further key component is the role of symmetry between the nodes and their interconnections, as it is symmetry that lies at the heart of the Buridan's ass puzzle. In the classical Buridan's ass paradox it is symmetry between competing alternatives that freezes the ass into indecision. In the quantum case, however, interference results in a far richer dynamics.

items.title_en: Looking Beyond Visibility: Resolving the Temporal Structure of Continuous-Wave Four-Photon Hong-Ou-Mandel Interference
items.abstract_en: Hong-Ou-Mandel interference underpins many photonic quantum information protocols and is commonly characterized by a single visibility parameter. This quantity is typically obtained by averaging over a fixed coincidence window, thereby discarding details of the underlying temporal structure that are critical in continuous-wave processes. Four-photon interference with continuous-wave sources furthermore requires photon pairs with long coherence times, which we generate in microring resonators and measure with ultrafast time-resolved detection. Here, we model and resolve their interference and temporal structure by recording all four photon arrival times and mapping their relative delays onto a three-dimensional coincidence histogram relative to a trigger detection. The resulting structure preserves relative arrival-time correlations that are usually discarded and enables post-processed optimization of coincidence windows to trade off visibility against count rate. This method provides a general benchmark for continuous-wave sources in interference-based quantum network protocols.

items.title_en: Selected Stabilizer Subspaces for Compact Many-Body Wave Functions
items.abstract_en: Selected configuration interaction (SCI) obtains accurate many-body solutions by variationally diagonalising the Hamiltonian in a sparse, iteratively selected set of configurations, but can lose compactness when the target state has broad configurational support. We introduce selected stabilizer interaction (SSI), a fully classical, SCI-inspired method that instead iteratively constructs a nonorthogonal subspace spanned by a systematically enlargeable set of selected stabilizer states. A single stabilizer, generated by Clifford operations, can encode a structured superposition of (possibly exponentially) many configurations, shifting the relevant compression from configurational to stabilizer sparsity. We benchmark ground-state energies, fidelities, superposition degrees and required expansion lengths against exact diagonalization and equivalent SCI schemes for the transverse-field Ising, XXZ Heisenberg, and Hubbard models, finding particularly strong compression from the stabilizer representation in the spin models, and increasing advantage with system size for these systems. The results establish a proof of principle for heuristic selected stabilizer diagonalization, while also identifying particular challenges in symmetry handling and effective exploration of the stabilizer space.

items.title_en: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Optimization for Emergency-Priority Traffic Signal Control
items.abstract_en: Emergency-priority traffic signal control requires reducing emergency-vehicle delay while limiting disruption to ordinary traffic. This work investigates a finite-horizon QUBO formulation and compares Exact QUBO optimization, QAOA, CVaR-QAOA, a quantum machine-learning policy, fixed-time control, and max-pressure control in a three-intersection corridor. The study evaluates three traffic-demand regimes, examines the effect of the emergency-priority weight, and compares quantum solutions with the exact QUBO optimum. The optimization-based controllers achieved reliable emergency progression across all tested demand regimes, while max-pressure produced lower ordinary-traffic delay. Increasing emergency priority reduced emergency travel time but increased congestion, with diminishing improvements at larger weights. CVaR-QAOA reproduced the exact QUBO solution more accurately than standard QAOA, although the resulting differences in closed-loop traffic performance were comparatively small.

items.title_en: One generation of the Standard Model as a quantum error-correcting code
items.abstract_en: Together with a right-handed neutrino, the fermions of one generation of the Standard Model are labelled by five bits, a combinatorial structure tied to anomaly cancellation. We make this precise. Anomaly cancellation is the vanishing of a cubic form, the defining property of triorthogonal codes, the quantum error-correcting codes behind magic state distillation. Removing the right-handed neutrino gives a $[[15,1,3]]_p$ code for every prime $p$, including the Bravyi-Kitaev code for $p = 2$. For qutrits it is the unique shortest distance-three triorthogonal code.

items.title_en: Optical Coherent Combining in Multi-Aperture Free-Space Receivers through Atmospheric Turbulence via Optically Computed Alignment Gradients
items.abstract_en: Multi-aperture reception converts spatial diversity into a coherent-combining gain, but only if the relative phase and polarization of the collected field replicas are aligned before they are summed. In a satellite-to-ground downlink the atmosphere perturbs amplitude, phase and polarization, so the alignment must track a fluctuating channel rather than a fixed offset. This paper proposes a new optical-domain combining scheme in which the alignment information is computed by light itself: the ascent directions that maximize the combined output power are formed by optical interference and read out directly as differential photocurrents of balanced detection, so no estimate of the channel, no deliberate perturbation, and no per-branch digital processing is needed to obtain them. Every branch is aligned against one shared reference - a passive tap of the combined field itself - so no independent laser or optical frequency lock is required, and the update directions of all branches are available simultaneously in a single averaging window without frequency, code, or time multiplexing. The data path needs a single dual-polarization coherent receiver regardless of the aperture count, and the readout is built from elementary parts only - a 3 dB directional coupler, static phase shifters, a Faraday rotator, and balanced photodiodes - so no 90-degree optical hybrid, mixer, or polarization-diverse hybrid is required. The phase and polarization loops are fixed-gain and division-free, and each branch carries one phase modulator and one polarization controller with no amplitude actuator. A closed-form combining-gain and loss budget is derived, the assumptions and limitations of the scheme are stated explicitly, and experimental validation remains open.

items.title_en: Microwave spectroscopic evidence of a moiré-commensurate electron crystal in monolayer graphene
items.abstract_en: We probe the conductivity of the lowest Landau level of a moiré-aligned monolayer graphene device by broadband microwave transmission through a coplanar waveguide ($\sim$50 mK, 15.4--18 T), isolating the longitudinal channel through a low-minus-high frequency band difference $D(ν)$. We resolve a series of minima in $D(ν)$ that drift with field along lines of fixed carrier density rather than fixed Landau filling, the hallmark of moiré-commensurate electron crystals. The strongest minimum is present at every field and matches no fractional quantum Hall or integer Hofstadter state. It lies at band filling $s=1/3$, one electron for every three moiré cells---the generalized Wigner crystal that DaSilva, Jung, and MacDonald predict as the most favorable fixed-density ($t=0$) commensuration. The weaker minima fall near neighboring commensurate fillings.

items.title_en: Superconducting circuits host two-level systems with lifetimes exceeding one second
items.abstract_en: Understanding the microscopic environment of superconducting qubits is a central challenge for quantum technologies. Parasitic two-level systems (TLSs) of various microscopic origins are ubiquitous and limit qubit performance through decoherence, frequency drifts, and leakage. Recently, long-lived TLSs with lifetimes exceeding those of state-of-the-art qubits have been shown to induce correlated qubit dynamics, with direct implications for quantum error correction. Here, we perform wide-band quantum-jump correlation spectroscopy on flux-tunable transmon qubits and identify microscopic degrees of freedom that outlive the qubit by orders of magnitude. Pump-probe measurements at varying detunings from these objects reveal intrinsic lifetimes exceeding one second. Their weak coupling to the qubit, in the kilohertz range, is consistent with positional defects described by the standard tunneling model, without excluding other microscopic origins such as magnetic spin impurities or trapped quasiparticles. More broadly, these results establish superconducting qubits as a sensitive probe of exceptionally long-lived microscopic degrees of freedom and open a route toward their controlled access and functionalization.

items.title_en: Ablation-Driven Selective Laser Direct Mass Transfer for Micro-LEDs with High Speed, Enhanced Gap Tolerance, and High Precision
items.title_zh: 面向Micro-LED的烧蚀驱动选择性激光直接质量转移：高速、增强间隙容差与高精度
items.abstract_en: Micro light-emitting diodes (micro-LEDs) offer superior performance for next-generation displays, yet their scalable manufacturing is severely bottlenecked by the mass transfer process from donor to receiver substrates. The existing laser-induced forward transfer (LIFT) methods are restricted by low throughput, limited selectivity, and long reaction times. In this study, we introduce a novel defocused direct laser ablation transfer (D-DLAT) method utilizing polyimide as a dynamic release layer. Whereas most indirect laser transfer methods trigger chip release followed by passive descent toward the receiver, D-DLAT directly ablates the release layer to actively propel the small-sized chips towards the receiver via ablation shock. By optimizing the ablation profiles and scanning paths, this method achieves high-speed transfer with significantly enhanced precision and robustness. We demonstrate the successful transfer of micro-LEDs ranging from 600 $\unicode{x03BC}$m down to 35 $\unicode{x03BC}$m in size, with a minimum reported placement error of less than 1 $\unicode{x03BC}$m, and a critical transfer gap of up to 50 $\unicode{x03BC}$m. Furthermore, the D-DLAT approach enables full selectivity, facilitating complex patterned transfers and array repitching operations that are essential for full-color display integration. Our findings indicate that D-DLAT effectively overcomes the fundamental limitations of current transfer technologies, demonstrating substantial potential for the scalable and high-yield manufacturing of advanced micro-LED displays. Ultimately, D-DLAT establishes a robust paradigm for the high-speed manipulation and heterogeneous integration of micro-optoelectronic devices, extending its profound implications beyond displays to the broader landscape of advanced micro-assembly and flexible electronics.

items.title_en: Three-axis Active Magnetic Compensation with Spatial Feedforward Matrix Decoupling and Hysteresis PI Regulation for Suppressing Zeeman Decoherence of Cold Atom Quantum Memories
items.abstract_en: Cold-atom quantum memories require a near-zero magnetic environment (residual field <1 microtesla) to mitigate Zeeman decoherence. Conventional three-axis active compensation suffers from inter-coil crosstalk and geomagnetic drift, which degrade the uniformity and long-term stability of the zero-field region. To address this, we propose a spatiotemporally cooperative feedback-controlled suppression architecture for magnetic interference. An integrally printed three-dimensional orthogonal coil frame mechanically suppresses inter-axis flux leakage. A spatial feedforward inverse matrix is introduced to algorithmically eliminate first-order cross-coupling. A dual-threshold hysteresis incremental-PI controller filters magnetometer quantization fluctuations and avoids frequent small jitter adjustments of coil driving currents. Hardware ablation experiments, long-duration stability tests and spatial magnetic-field mapping were conducted. Experimental results show that during a 714.4 s continuous steady-hold stage, the mean and maximum residual fields at the central point reach 0.112 microtesla and 0.224 microtesla, respectively. The overlapping Allan deviations of all three components remain below 5 nT for averaging times of 1.9-178.2 s. Based on differential-ferrofluid lattice-scan measurements combined with centre-constrained quadratic vector reconstruction and soft Maxwell regularization, a weak-field spatial distribution with an RMS variation of 5.65 microtesla is fitted within a spherical region of interest of radius 5 mm, where 67.5% of the model volume meets the sub-5 microtesla coverage criterion. For a prolate ellipsoidal region matching the atomic-cloud distribution with full axis lengths of 10, 5, and 5 mm, the upper field bound within 93.7% of the volume is 2.68 microtesla.

items.title_en: Controlled-Memory Identification with Shared Generators: Dimension--Horizon Tradeoffs and Quantum--Classical Separation
items.abstract_en: We determine the finite-horizon identification limits of a \(d\)-dimensional memory when the control interface is restricted to four shared, time-homogeneous generators. A writer encodes a message by applying a prefix word to a common root state. The verifier then applies a candidate-dependent query word followed by a shared terminal binary test, with each word of length at most \(T\). For fixed error tolerances \(λ_2>0\) and \(λ_1+λ_2<1\), the optimal identification sizes satisfy \(\ln N_{\mathsf Q,4}=Θ_{λ_1,λ_2}(\min\{d^2,T\})\) for arbitrary CPTP generators and \(\ln N_{\mathsf S,4}=Θ_{λ_1,λ_2}(\min\{d,T\})\) for stochastic maps. Four unitary letters and four permutation letters attain these respective bounds, showing that a four-letter reversible alphabet reaches the static code-size orders in optimal quadratic and linear word length. In the fully dimension-limited regime, this yields \(\ln N_{\mathsf Q,4}=Θ(d^2)\) versus \(\ln N_{\mathsf S,4}=Θ(d)\), establishing a quadratic quantum--classical separation in logarithmic code size. Low-overlap Grassmann and agreement-code packings supply the orbit endpoints, while exact inverse query words match each encoded state to its designated test. At the sharp boundary \(λ_2=0\), \(0\leqλ_1<1\), all four model classes satisfy \(\ln N=Θ(\min\{\ln d,T\})\). Thus any fixed positive false-acceptance tolerance activates the metric-packing regime, whereas zero false acceptance imposes an exclusive-witness constraint and yields the logarithmic-dimension boundary.

items.title_en: Quantum-compatible Riemannian conjugate gradient for ground-state preparation
items.abstract_en: Riemannian optimization provides a natural geometric framework for designing quantum algorithms for ground-state preparation, most notably through quantum imaginary-time evolution. However, existing geometry-aware approaches primarily employ steepest-descent updates, leaving more advanced methods from classical Riemannian optimization largely unexplored. In this work, we introduce quantum conjugate gradient descent (QCGD), a quantum-compatible implementation of Riemannian conjugate gradient that combines the steepest descent direction with information retained from previous search directions. In our numerical experiments, the proposed approach achieves faster convergence per iteration than the baseline double-bracket quantum imaginary-time evolution (DB-QITE) algorithm, and we quantify the associated circuit cost with gate counts produced by Qrisp. This improvement, however, comes at the cost of increased circuit depth for each update step, revealing a trade-off between convergence rate and implementation complexity. Nevertheless, since the circuit depth for those algorithms grows exponentially with the number of iterations, the proposed method may offer practical advantages, particularly in the early fault-tolerant regime.

items.title_en: Same Spectrum, Harder First-Order Training: Phase-Locking in Single- versus Multi-Qubit Re-Uploading Circuits
items.title_zh: 相同频谱，更难的一阶训练：单量子比特与多量子比特重上传电路中的锁相
items.abstract_en: Angle-encoded variational quantum circuits implement truncated Fourier series. For one-dimensional inputs, a single-qubit re-uploading (serial) circuit represents every function that a multi-qubit circuit with the same encoding budget $E$ can; we find that this exchange of width for depth is not free in first-order training. Because its state lives on the Bloch sphere, all parameters of the serial circuit move the state, at each input, along one complex direction, which we call \emph{phase-locking}. We prove that this costs no Fourier direction but leaves no direction to spare: however many parameters it has, the serial circuit has at most $2E+2$ tangent directions, one more than its $2E+1$ Fourier coefficients need, while a two-qubit control with the same encoding budget and model class generically has at least $6E+6$. The cost in training is measured against this control, as the number of runs out of 100 that reach the optimum within a fixed step budget. On an exact loss with flat-spectrum targets the gap grows with $E$; at $E=32$ the serial circuit converges in 3, 53 and 83 runs under gradient descent, Adam and Levenberg--Marquardt, the control in 99, 100 and 100. On three real-world series, at matched parameter counts, the serial circuit reaches the least-squares optimum in at most 9 runs under Adam and in 32 to 93 under Levenberg--Marquardt, the control in at least 98 and in all 100; its held-out error is up to about $1.5$ times that of the control under Adam, but no larger in the typical run under Levenberg--Marquardt.

items.title_en: Watt-level single-cavity dual-comb laser at 2.1 $μ$m wavelength
items.abstract_en: Compact ultrafast laser combs around the 2 $μ$m atmospheric transmission window are of growing interest for direct spectroscopy and as drivers for nonlinear conversion to otherwise hard-to-reach spectral regions. Dual-comb systems in this region remain very scarce: existing implementations rely mostly on nonlinear conversion, resulting in complex systems with poor conversion efficiency and overall low average and peak power. In this paper, we report on a watt-level dual-comb laser directly emitting at 2.1 $μ$m. The system is based on a single-cavity, soft-aperture Kerr-lens mode-locked (KLM) laser using a broadband holmium (Ho)-doped CaAlGdO$_4$ (CALGO) gain crystal. The laser delivers a total output power exceeding 2 W (1 W per comb) with a sub-100-fs pulse duration (50 nm bandwidth) at a repetition rate of 96.5 MHz, corresponding to a pulse energy of 10 nJ and a peak power of 100 kW per comb. To assess the source's potential for future spectroscopic applications, we characterize the free-running dual comb in detail for frequency stability, phase noise, and relative intensity noise (RIN), and benchmark the achievable spectral resolution by measuring spectral modulations imposed by Fabry-Pérot etalons. Our system combines the compactness, high efficiency, and passive mutual coherence of a single-cavity oscillator with watt-level average power at 2.1 $μ$m, making it a promising source for environmental sensing in the atmospheric transmission window, or as a driver for nonlinear frequency conversion, for example, to the MIR and THz regions.

items.title_en: Local finite rate semi device independent randomness expansion from quantum contextuality
items.abstract_en: Finite rate randomness expansion (RE) which is secure against quantum adversaries is a crucial information processing task which is well studied in the case of two non-communicating parties sharing Bell non-local correlations in a device independent manner. In this paper we show that contextual correlations with only a single localized party are sufficient for RE in a semi-device independent (SDI) manner. We propose a template SDI-RE protocol which is applicable for arbitrary $N$-cycle non-contextuality (NC) inequalities and derive its RE rate under finite statistics. As a special case, we also highlight the advantages of the situation when RE is constrained by Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality but with characterized measurements implemented by only a single party. Our template protocol also incorporates non-ideal statistics which may not satisfy perfect commutativity and perfect repeatability, both of which are necessary in a loophole-free test of NC inequalities. As such, several recent experimental implementations of significantly loophole-free tests of NC inequalities can be modified for secure RE following our approach.

items.title_en: Probing Deconfined Quantum Criticality Point on a Digital Quantum Computer
items.abstract_en: A deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) is a continuous transition between ordered phases with unrelated broken symmetries, beyond the Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm. In one dimension, such a transition between a $z$-polarized ferromagnet (zFM) and a valence-bond solid (VBS) is well established numerically in a frustrated spin-$1/2$ chain. Here we ask whether a superconducting quantum processor can resolve this transition and its signatures despite finite-size effects and device noise. The ground states are prepared by ancilla-projected quantum imaginary-time evolution (QITE), whose exact target states are compressed by tensor-network optimization into shallow depth quantum circuits. The hardware data distinguish the phases through their order parameters, spin and dimer correlations, structure factors, correlation ratios, and snapshot distributions. The crossing of the order parameters locates the transition, and its finite-size extrapolation lies close to the thermodynamic-limit value obtained from large-scale numerics. A noise model based on the device calibration accounts quantitatively for the reduced amplitudes measured on hardware. Our findings demonstrate that a Landau-forbidden transition between competing orders can be resolved on current quantum processors.

items.title_en: Remote Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Entanglement Generation between Trapped Ions
items.abstract_en: Distributing entanglement directly between error-corrected logical qubits is an important capability for scalable quantum networks. We propose a heralded protocol for generating remote entanglement between Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill qubits encoded in the motional modes of spatially separated trapped ions, using the internal electronic states to interface the motional qubits with emitted photons. We derive the protocol for single-rail and polarization photonic encodings and evaluate the effects of finite GKP squeezing, photon loss, photon recoil, motional heating, and motional dephasing on the decoded logical state. Moreover, we numerically analysed the fidelity of distributed logical Bell-pair fidelity. We find that one can achieve more than 95% of fidelity in the realistic situation. The protocol combines motional-control and photonic-networking operations that have already been demonstrated in trapped-ion experiments.

items.title_en: Mosaic: Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.title_zh: Mosaic：多会话智能体强化学习
items.abstract_en: Most existing agentic reinforcement learning methods assume single-session trajectories, where interaction proceeds within one continuously accumulated context. However, agentic techniques such as context compaction and subagent forking may produce trajectories spanning multiple sessions, creating a mismatch between the single-session training assumption and inference-time execution. Therefore, we introduce Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning, a more general setting that supports an arbitrary number of sessions within a trajectory. Under this setting, a widely adopted method is to broadcast trajectory-level advantages to all sessions, but this does not distinguish contributions from various sessions or guide session allocation within trajectories. To address this issue, we propose Mosaic, a multi-session agentic RL method with critic-free hierarchical optimization. At the trajectory level, it incorporates session-usage signals into advantage estimation. At the session level, it shapes each session's advantage according to the estimated marginal contribution. Experiments on BrowseComp with Qwen3.5-4B show that Mosaic outperforms broadcasting in both context compaction and subagent forking scenarios while using fewer sessions on average. Further analyses show that our method achieves improvements in session utility and allocation, which we suggested is a promising target for future advances in multi-session agentic RL.
items.abstract_zh: 现有智能体强化学习多假设单会话轨迹，但上下文压缩、子代理分叉等技术会产生跨多个会话的轨迹，造成训练假设与推理执行不匹配。为此，本文提出多会话智能体强化学习设置，支持一条轨迹内任意数量会话。针对将轨迹级优势广播到所有会话无法区分各会话贡献的问题，提出Mosaic：无评论家的分层优化方法，在轨迹级把会话使用信号纳入优势估计，在会话级按估计的边际贡献塑形优势。在BrowseComp与Qwen3.5-4B上的实验表明，Mosaic在上下文压缩和子代理分叉场景均优于广播方法，且平均使用更少会话。
items.highlight_zh: 分层无评论家优化按会话边际贡献分配优势
items.digest_zh: 研究问题：多数智能体强化学习假设单会话轨迹，但上下文压缩和子代理分叉会让轨迹跨越多个会话，导致训练与推理不匹配；直接把轨迹级优势广播给所有会话，也无法区分各会话贡献或指导会话分配。方法：提出多会话智能体强化学习设置，并给出Mosaic，一种无评论家的分层优化方法。轨迹级把会话使用信号纳入优势估计；会话级根据估计的边际贡献调整每个会话的优势。结果：在BrowseComp任务和Qwen3.5-4B模型上，Mosaic在上下文压缩与子代理分叉两种场景都优于广播基线，同时平均使用更少会话。进一步分析显示会话效用和会话分配均有改善。意义：为多会话智能体提供更细粒度的信用分配，指出会话效用与分配是未来改进的重要方向。

items.title_en: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
items.title_zh: MLExpert：面向自主机器学习工程的通用智能体模型
items.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI (AI4AI) as a pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). Workflow-driven machine learning engineering (MLE) systems provide a practical path toward this pursuit through complex orchestration that manages long-horizon experimentation, while recent MLE systems adopt model-directed interaction, allowing models to autonomously organize experiments and adapt optimization strategies based on execution feedback. However, feedback from each experiment reflects several preceding decisions, and a long MLE run contains many such costly experiments. Training must therefore select useful supervision from long interaction trajectories and learn from intermediate outcomes. We propose a post-training method for autonomous long-horizon MLE optimization and apply it to train MLExpert, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model. We design the Kaggle-MLE Factory to construct executable tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation. Hierarchical agentic SFT transfers general tool-use and coding capabilities to MLE through outcome-guided supervision. Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) treats the multi-turn decisions between successive experiment results as an execution window and assigns it a shared outcome-based reward. Asynchronous collection and policy correction support policy updates before the trajectory ends. On MLE-Bench Lite, MLExpert improves the average medal rate of the base model from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving performance comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3. Further experiments show that MLExpert improves performance on NatureBench Lite, agent scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization, suggesting that the learned optimization capability generalizes to other tasks.
items.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLM）正从辅助科研与工程，走向自主开发并改进 AI 系统，即“AI for AI”（AI4AI），被视为通向递归自我改进（RSI）的路径。工作流驱动的机器学习工程（MLE）系统通过管理长程实验的复杂编排提供了可行途径，近期的 MLE 系统更采用模型主导的交互方式，让模型自主组织实验并依据执行反馈调整优化策略。然而，每次实验的反馈都耦合了此前若干决策，且一次长程 MLE 运行包含大量昂贵实验，因此训练必须从长交互轨迹中筛选有用监督并利用中间结果学习。我们提出一种面向自主长程 MLE 优化的后训练方法，并据此训练出 MLExpert——一个 35B 混合专家（MoE）智能体模型。我们设计了 Kaggle-MLE Factory 来构建可执行任务与模型主导实验的交互框架。分层智能体 SFT 通过结果引导的监督，将通用工具使用与编程能力迁移到 MLE；窗口化交互强化学习（WIRL）把相邻实验结果之间的多轮决策视为一个执行窗口，并赋予共享的基于结果的奖励；异步采集与策略校正支持在轨迹结束前更新策略。在 MLE-Bench Lite 上，MLExpert 将基座模型的平均奖牌率从 37.9% 提升至 72.7%，与 Kimi-K3、GLM-5.3 等更大规模的前沿模型表现相当。
items.highlight_zh: 用窗口化交互强化学习训练 35B 智能体，奖牌率翻倍至 72.7%
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：如何让 AI 自主完成端到端的机器学习工程（MLE）——自己写代码、跑实验、看结果、再改进，而不是只做单步辅助。难点在于一次 MLE 长跑包含许多昂贵实验，而每个实验的结果都由前面一连串决策共同造成，奖励信号“归因”困难，不能简单当成单轮任务来训练。

方法：作者训练了一个 35B 的混合专家（MoE）智能体模型 MLExpert。先搭建 Kaggle-MLE Factory，把真实竞赛转成可执行、可交互的任务环境；再用分层智能体 SFT，把通用的工具调用与编程能力迁移到 MLE 场景；核心创新是窗口化交互强化学习（WIRL）：把两次实验结果之间的多轮动作打包成一个“执行窗口”，给整个窗口一个共享的、基于最终结果的奖励，从而绕开逐步归因难题。配合异步采集与策略校正，模型在轨迹尚未结束时就可持续更新。

结果：在 MLE-Bench Lite 上，平均奖牌率从基座模型的 37.9% 提升到 72.7%，与规模更大的前沿模型 Kimi-K3、GLM-5.3 相当。论文还报告在 NatureBench Lite、智能体脚手架优化等任务上的提升。

为何重要：它说明中等规模开源模型只要在“长程交互”这一层做对训练，就能在真实工程任务上逼近大模型，为 AI 自主改进 AI（AI4AI）提供了可落地的训练范式。

items.title_en: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
items.title_zh: PathFM：多元轨迹的快速生成式预测
items.abstract_en: Time series foundation models are becoming increasingly popular for general-purpose forecasting. However, most leading models predict marginal quantiles, leaving the dependence structure of future trajectories unspecified. This distinction matters for trajectory-dependent quantities such as cumulative demand, peak load, and event timing, yet point and marginal scores do not reveal it. To model this dependence, we introduce PathFM, a trajectory-based forecasting model that uses flow matching to generate complete future paths. We further distill the model to one or two steps and share history attention cache across draws.
